newsitem.title: USA: Report said to admit Polish-Swiss deal on assets.
newsitem.headline: Report said to admit Polish-Swiss deal on assets.

text.p: Switzerland will report later this week it gave Poland unclaimed Swiss bank accounts -- much of it belonging to Holocaust victims -- in 1949 and then Poland used some of that money to compensate Swiss citizens, a World Jewish Congress offical said on Monday.

The official, WJC vice president Kalman Sultanik, said the admission would be contained in a report from the Swiss Foreign Ministry on deals made between Berne and Warsaw to settle claims by Swiss citizens for the nationalisation of their property after the communists took control.
Jewish groups have strongly protested Switzerland's transfer of heirless Polish assets in Swiss banks, saying that much of it came from accounts set up by Jews who died in the Holocaust.
Sultanik, basing his comments on information received from Switzerland, said Berne paid Warsaw "hundreds of thousands of Swiss francs" in the 1970s to complete the 1949 agreement.
He added that a small amount of that money was then used by Poland to then settle claims made against it by Swiss citizens.
Sultanik, who has been strongly critical of Swiss failure to return Jewish assets, said, "This was an immoral transfer of money that was deposited by those murdered by the Nazis."
He noted that Switzerland had failed to give Poland the names of the people whose assets were being transferred, making it impossible for Poland to return the funds to legitimate claimants or heirs.
